questions.question: Which living organism is considered one of the oldest known individual trees on Earth?
questions.hint: Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine in California, is estimated to be over 4,800 years old, making it one of the oldest known non-clonal living trees.

questions.question: Which animal has the highest number of teeth among mammals?
questions.hint: The Giant Armadillo can have up to 100 teeth, the most of any living land mammal.

questions.question: Which film became the first sequel to win the Academy Award for Best Picture?
questions.hint: Released in 1974, The Godfather Part II made history as the first sequel to win Best Picture.

questions.question: Which fictional city is protected by Batman?
questions.hint: Batman has defended Gotham City since his first comic appearance in 1939.

questions.question: Which organization awards the Nobel Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, and Medicine?
questions.hint: The Royal Swedish Academy awards the Physics and Chemistry prizes, while the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute awards the Medicine prize.

questions.question: Which international day is observed on December 10 each year?
questions.hint: Human Rights Day commemorates the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.

questions.question: Which empire built the famous city of Persepolis?
questions.hint: Persepolis was founded by Darius I around 518 BC as the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.

questions.question: Which navigator became the first known European to reach the Pacific Ocean by crossing the Isthmus of Panama?
questions.hint: In 1513, Balboa became the first recorded European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas.

questions.question: Which nation has won the most ICC Champions Trophy titles (including shared titles)?
questions.hint: India has won the ICC Champions Trophy twice outright and shared one title in 2002.

questions.question: In athletics, how long is an Olympic marathon?
questions.hint: The marathon distance has been standardized at 42.195 kilometers (26 miles 385 yards) since 1921.

questions.question: Which country contains the world's largest delta?
questions.hint: The Ganges–Brahmaputra–Meghna Delta, mostly in Bangladesh, is the world's largest river delta.

questions.question: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
questions.hint: The Bering Strait separates Russia and Alaska at their closest point.

questions.question: Which physicist discovered electromagnetic induction?
questions.hint: Faraday's discovery of electromagnetic induction made electric generators and transformers possible.

questions.question: Which SI unit measures luminous intensity?
questions.hint: The candela is one of the seven base SI units and measures luminous intensity.

questions.question: Which civilization built the monumental statues known as Moai?
questions.hint: The Moai statues were carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island between the 13th and 16th centuries.

questions.question: Which country is the birthplace of the philosopher Confucius?
questions.hint: Confucius was born in the ancient Chinese state of Lu around 551 BC.

questions.question: Which species is the largest living marsupial?
questions.hint: Adult male Red Kangaroos can exceed 90 kg (200 lb) and stand over 2 meters tall.

questions.question: Which country has the highest average elevation above sea level?
questions.hint: Bhutan's mountainous terrain gives it the highest average elevation of any sovereign country.

questions.question: Which scientist is known as the "Father of Genetics"?
questions.hint: Mendel's experiments with pea plants established the basic principles of heredity.

questions.question: Which civilization created the world's earliest known written legal code, the Code of Ur-Nammu?
questions.hint: The Code of Ur-Nammu, dating to around 2100–2050 BC, is the oldest surviving known law code.
